page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the e2-highmem-4 delivers modest processing capabilities. CPU-bound workloads, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, fall into the bottom 25% of performance. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores rank in the bottom 10%, with poor performance observed in text processing, image processing, and file compression tasks. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in PassMark memory tests and small-model LLM text generation, while memory bandwidth and database operations remain in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the e2-highmem-4 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance compute. The primary tradeoff is the pairing of a generous 32.0 GB memory allocation with a relatively weak CPU subsystem, which limits its utility for compute-intensive tasks like software compilation or ray tracing.

This instance configuration is suitable for memory-intensive but CPU-light workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale database hosting, caching layers, lightweight enterprise applications, and basic text generation tasks utilizing small language models.
